headlines.text: Police hiring standards matter. But they alone cannot stop abuse. Law enforcement in the US needs high hiring standards. But it also needs reform and trust-building in communities.
Jerusalem Daily: Gaza’s children return to schools. It's the first official day back to school for Gaza's children.
Djibouti refugee crisis worsens as more than 2,700 Yemenis arrive. More than 2,700 Yemenis have fled to Djibouti, many making dangerous sea crossings to escape the conflict.
Russia reports ‘powerful’ cyberattacks on second day of parliamentary vote. This is Russia's first election since it invaded Ukraine, and is expected to gauge public support for the ongoing war.

Mountain lion caught on camera evading capture in San Francisco before being tranquilized, released. A mountain lion was tranquilized in San Francisco's Sunset District after evading capture for hours. It was later released back into the wild.

Cuba plunges into total blackout as electrical grid collapses again, US Embassy warns. Cuba's entire electrical grid collapsed Friday, triggering a nationwide blackout with cellphone and internet outages reported across the island.

Yankees star Aaron Judge heads back to injured list weeks after returning from broken rib. Aaron Judge heads to the New York Yankees injured list with a right calf strain that could sideline the three-time AL MVP for the rest of the season.

Why the House let out early is a matter of debate after Johnson says chamber has 'done its work'. Thomas Massie claims Mike Johnson sent the House home early to dodge a vote on his eight privileged impeachment articles against Pete Hegseth.

Hiker, 61, battles agonizing injury on grueling climb, resets dislocated shoulder himself. Kurt Siuzdak slipped on wet granite on New Hampshire's Mount Washington, dislocated his shoulder, popped it back in and kept climbing to the top.

Paramount appears to learn from its 'Big Brother' racial double standard on 'The Challenge'. Three contestants were removed from MTV's "The Challenge: Cutthroat" after a reported racial incident involving the N-word and a code of conduct breach.
